N° 20Educational simulation game: agriculture, trade and network engineering2026

Racines & Réseaux

A pixel-art simulation game set in Cameroon that combines farming, regional trade and the social life of the Bandjoun Kingdom with network-troubleshooting laboratories in which the player restores connectivity to schools and cooperatives.

Visit the site ↗How to useIn motion

01

Problem statement

Farming simulations are popular worldwide but are almost never set in Africa, and fewer still convey accurate knowledge about it. Young Cameroonians abroad know little of the crops, crafts, markets and customs of their parents’ villages, and network engineering is seldom presented as a trade capable of changing a village.

02

Contribution

The player clears, tills, sows, waters and harvests on the grandfather’s farm in the Centre, then travels to the Bandjoun Kingdom in the West: the chefferie and its great hut, the market of the eight-day week, the artisans’ quarter, the coffee cooperative and the family compound. Trade extends to Bafoussam, Foumban, Douala, Penja and Yaoundé; crops are processed into goods of higher value; the player joins a tontine and attends funerals, a dowry ceremony and festivals. Network laboratories present a real fault, such as a school without Internet access, and score the diagnostic method as well as the result.

03

Architecture

Godot 4 in GDScript. Every crop, item, recipe, market, character, quest and article is stored as bilingual JSON data, separate from the engine code. Pixel art and audio are original and produced by Python scripts.

04

Method and data

A network simulator models DHCP, DNS, NAT, VLANs and Wi-Fi for the laboratories. Automated tests replay the whole story from the first quest to confirm that no quest can become blocked.

05

Verification and limitations

The rulers in the story are fictional, and sacred rites are shown only from the outside. The current build is a playable test version for the browser and Windows; a Steam release is planned.
